The '''1962–63 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|60th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|31st consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

Real Madrid secured a record 9th Primera División title surpassing Barcelona for most league title wins. The club also became the first to win three consecutive league titles.

==Summary==
Owing to a disappointing performance of Spain in the [[1962 FIFA World Cup]], the Spanish Federation imposed a ban on the transfers of foreign players, with the measure lasting 11 years until 1973 with [[oriundo]] players exemptions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/05/26/reportajes/1590459438_017479.html|publisher=as.com|title=A League of Foreigners|language=es|author=Ignacio Camacho|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> During the summer midfielder [[Luis Del Sol]] was sold to [[Juventus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0221-0e9b40d7321f-bd6b5a292ddc-1000--players-and-coaches-who-unite-juve-and-madrid/|title=Players and coaches who unite Juve and Madrid|publisher=UEFA|date=5 May 2015|access-date=9 March 2020}}</ref> The club transferred in defender [[Ignacio Zoco]] from Osasuna an arrival to reinforce the back-up line.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/zoco-in-ec.html|title= Ignacio Zoco Esparza  Matches in European Cups|publisher= Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation}}</ref> The transitional stage in the club continued with new arrivals such as right winger [[Amancio Amaro]] Nicknamed 'The Wizard' from [[Deportivo La Coruña]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2012/09/07/mas_futbol/1346999214_850215.html |publisher=Diario As |access-date=10 November 2016 |title=Se cumplen 50 años del debut del 'Brujo Amancio'|language=es}}</ref> French midfielder [[Lucien Muller]] (Di Stefano saw him during a Spain-France match and asked him to play in Real Madrid)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2006/05/10/mas_futbol/1147242425_850215.html|publisher=as.com|title=En realidad fue Di Stefano quien me fichó|language=es}}</ref> slovak [[Yanko Daucik]]<ref>{{Cite book|last=Jose|first=Colin|title=On-Side – 125 Years of Soccer in Ontario|publisher=Ontario Soccer Association and Soccer Hall of Fame and Museum|year=2001|location=Vaughan, Ontario|pages=197}}</ref> and [[FC Barcelona]] Brazilian forward [[Evaristo de Macedo]].<ref>{{Cite news | last = Buturugeanu| first = Alex | title = Tradatorii (IV): Tejada & Macedo | newspaper = [[Istoria Fotbalului]] | date = 17 October 2010 | url = http://www.istoriafotbalului.com/tradatorii-iv-tejada-macedo/ | access-date = 17 October 2010 | location=Bucharest}}</ref>

The club repeated defended its La Liga title from the previous season, its ninth overall, also marking Real Madrid's first ever [[Three-peat#Spain|three-peat]]. The team finished 12 points above runners-up [[Atlético Madrid]]. In the Copa del Generalísimo, the squad reached the semi-finals where it was defeated by Zaragoza. In the European Cup, Madrid was eliminated in the preliminary round, surprisingly losing to Belgian squad [[RSC Anderlecht]]. Additionally, 36-years-old forward [[Ferenc Puskás]] again won the individual League top-scorer trophy with 26 goals.
